title: Assisted-living coverage and spending do not establish an affordable, available care setting
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107884; federal assisted-living spending, Medicaid coverage, and state waiver structure
geography: United States assisted-living facilities and state Medicaid programs for older adults and people with disabilities

observations.period: Calendar year 2024; federal Medicaid and traditional Medicare spending for services in assisted-living facilities

denominator.unit: at least dollars in identified federal Medicaid and Medicare spending for services provided in assisted-living facilities

federal_medicaid_spending.unit: at least dollars in federal Medicaid spending

traditional_medicare_spending.unit: dollars for covered health services delivered in assisted living, including services such as hospice

spending_boundary.value: likely undercount because assisted-living facilities are not uniformly defined or consistently identified in data

observations.method: GAO analysis of 2024 Medicaid and Medicare claims data, the most recent year available, with program documentation review.
observations.uncertainty: The $12 billion is a floor for identified services, not total assisted-living spending, resident out-of-pocket cost, room-and-board support, facility cost, quality, unmet need, or resident outcome; Medicare generally does not cover assisted-living services themselves.
observations.subgroup: Services delivered in assisted-living facilities and identified in federal Medicaid/Medicare claims; residents and facilities are not a uniform care or payer universe.
observations.counterinterpretation: A spending undercount can coexist with substantial service delivery and household protection; a larger public spending total would not by itself establish affordability, suitable placement, or better outcomes.

observations.period: As of March 2025; state Medicaid coverage of assisted-living services

denominator.unit: states assessed for Medicaid coverage of assisted-living services for older adults and people with disabilities

states_covering_services.unit: states with Medicaid coverage for assisted-living services

hcbs_waiver_states.unit: of the 44 covering states using Medicaid home- and community-based-services waivers

waiver_boundary.value: waivers can target populations and limit enrollment

observations.method: GAO review of state Medicaid program documents and coverage structures as of March 2025.
observations.uncertainty: State coverage is a policy measure, not eligible-person enrollment, authorized slots, provider participation, room-and-board affordability, wait time, service receipt, quality, or continuity when needs change.
observations.subgroup: Older adults and people with disabilities potentially eligible for state Medicaid assisted-living services.
observations.counterinterpretation: A state without this Medicaid service may use other home-, residential-, or state-funded routes; a waiver can target scarce resources while still leaving some people without a suitable slot.

denominator.unit: assisted-living residents and care bundles; no common resident-level affordability or access denominator

care_setting.value: assisted living is a residential alternative to in-home care and nursing homes for people needing help with activities of daily living

payer_split.value: Medicaid may cover assistance and supportive services; Medicare may cover other health care such as hospice; households commonly use personal resources; HUD and VA may help with room and board but amounts were unknown

data_gap.value: claims identify paid services but not all unmet needs, informal care, quality, resident choice, or later displacement

observations.method: GAO synthesis of claims, state coverage documents, federal program documentation, and assisted-living financing boundaries.
observations.uncertainty: The record does not observe search, eligibility, authorization, waitlist, admission, discharge, room/board payment, family labor, resident safety, work/time effect, or later setting choice in the same episode.
observations.subgroup: Residents and households navigating assisted living, home care, nursing homes, Medicaid, Medicare, HUD, VA, private payment, and informal support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mixed payer arrangements can provide flexible protection and resident choice; financial fragmentation may be manageable for some households and constraining for others depending on assets, family support, state, and provider supply.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies federal spending floor, Medicaid state coverage, waiver structure, financing boundaries, methods, and data limitations.

boundary: This record establishes assisted-living financing, Medicaid policy coverage, waiver, and care-bundle stages. It does not establish total spending, resident affordability, unmet need, wait time, available slots, provider capacity, quality, safety, health, family work/time, displacement, setting choice, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO HTML report page retrieved and hashed; report PDF, Medicaid/Medicare claims, state waiver archives, facility files, and resident microdata not retained
